claims.claim_text: Indexed George Vetlesen is probably the Norwegian-American OSS officer Georg Unger Vetlesen described by Columbia and Store norske leksikon.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon surname, George/Georg spelling variant, Navy commander context and responsibility for Norway in OSS London align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable rather than high confidence because the index omits rank and identifiers and the adjacent Frederick Vetlesen row remains separate.
claims.temporal_assessment: Institutional sources document wartime OSS service and a 1943 Navy entry, while the index file remains necessary for a definitive bridge.
claims.match_notes: George and Frederick Vetlesen remain separate person entities. No claim or affiliation is transferred between them.

claims.claim_text: The probable Georg Unger Vetlesen match worked for many years as a U.S. shipbuilder and naval engineer before entering the Navy in 1943.

claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable identity bridge from the uncommon name and matching OSS Norway role.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar occupation; no named employer or exact immediate-to-Navy sequence is supplied.
claims.match_notes: Published only as a qualified occupation, excluded from verified-employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Francis J Vicovari is probably the Francis J. Vicovari who led a British American Ambulance Corps unit in 1941.

research_attempts.query_text: George Vetlesen; NARA OSS index and official Archives context; CIA Reading Room or equivalent official-source check; exact-name and meaningful variants; OSS, Army, Navy, Marines, rank, branch and assignment clues; employer and occupation 1940; obituary, institutional, newspaper, directory, Library of Congress and archival searches; indexed Box 804; protected identifiers used only in private official-record comparison
